When and why did you start training for fighting? 16 years of age. A friend introduced me to Kickboxing at Fight Club Novi Sad, and the first rule about the fight club is that you don’t talk about fight club. 

What ranks and titles have you held? Champion of Serbia in K-1. Medalist in WAKO European Championships in Lignano Sabbiadorro, Italy. Medalist at World Cup Serbia Open in Belgrade. Multiple-time champion in several kickboxing disciplines in province of Vojvodina, Serbia. Judo orange belt, BJJ blue belt 

Do you have any heroes? There are people I admire, and as far as heroes the future me is my hero.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? This is a dream come true for me and my brother. We have been dreaming about this for many years. My friends and family that know me personally know that this was coming, and some of them have proof of me talking about being up there in the best promotion in the world. I have predicted the future for myself on several occasions; this is one of those occasions. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I studied Sports and Physical Education at the University of Novi Sad in Serbia. I moved to the United States before I got an opportunity to graduate. 

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked from making $2 or (200 Dinars) a day in a Betting office in Serbia, to serving in restaurants, mowing lawns in the United States, construction and selling cars at a dealership and full-time training, no matter what job I had. 

Favorite grappling technique: Stay off bottom

Favorite Striking technique: Kickboxing

qna.value:
TRAINING: Every day it changes, but usually I do sparring in the morning, conditioning in the afternoon and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu to finish the day.

 

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training years after the first UFC. I watched the Gracie family showcase their BJJ in the Octagon and I quickly became a fan. Then I realized that I wanted to learn the art of fighting and there was no other way but to learn BJJ with it. Eventually I found a BJJ gym in Florida, Team Popovitch, who helped guide me into my dreams today.

 

What ranks and titles have you held? Fight Time Lightweight Championship and ISKA Lightweight Championship. I also have lots of titles in BJJ such as: North American ADCC Trials Champion, 3rd Abu Dhabi World Pro Weight & Absolute, several times NAGA and Grapplers Quest Champion, Brown Belt Pan American Champion, 3rd Brown Belt Gi Worlds.

 

Do you have any heroes? I'm a really big fan of Renzo Gracie, Wanderlei Silva, Minotauro.

 

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means everything. It means I will have the chance to show people what I do best and to be recognized for my talent. I want to build a legacy, to be remembered and not quickly forgotten like a lot of other guys. That's why fighting in the UFC is so important to me because once I step into that Octagon, people will never forget me.

 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Only college I went to was the BRAZILIAN JIU JITSU CENTER, that's where I got my Black Belt degree.

 

What was your job before you started fighting? Back in the days I used to work in construction. Now I teach BJJ.

 

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Victory over Igor Gracie. It had to be a turning point in my MMA career.

 

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Second degree Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Black Belt

 

Favorite grappling technique: Full guard

 

Favorite striking technique: Straight right hand

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training Taekwondo when I was five years old because it’s a family tradition. My mother is the sportswoman of the family - she is a 3rd dan black belt in taekwondo. I have been training multiple disciplines since the early beginnings of my journey as a martial artist. My coach Pavel Fedotov has taught all his students mixed martial arts (what he called Universal Martial Arts) long before they were popular like today. Every time we trained, we practiced sambo, judo, wrestling, boxing, and taekwondo. Every week we competed in different styles and sometimes at two different events with different styles on the same day. I have been training mixed martial arts (MMA) since the beginning, and I started competing in MMA professionally in 2003.

Training: My days leading up to this fight start early in the morning.  Each day increases in intensity as we are now growing closer to the fight.  During the preparation, we are working on striking and grappling every day.  In the afternoon, I do additional conditioning outdoors.  Some days I do grueling conditioning in nature outside of the gym.

What ranks and titles have you held? Former UFC women’s flyweight champion. World Championship Titles (17-Time World Muay Thai and K1 Champion). Master of Sport International Class in Muay Thai, Master of Sport in Boxing (Russian Amateur National Champion), Kickboxing, Taekwondo and Judo

Do you have any heroes? My heroes are my family, my friends, and my supporters.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means having the opportunity to compete against the best fighters in the world.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? University of Arts Kyrgystan, Undergraduate Degree in Film Directing

What was your job before you started fighting? I have been a fighter in combat sports since the age of 12.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? IFMA (International Muay Thai Federation) Champion - 9 Times
 

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Record in Muay Thai / K-1 56-2. Combined professional record of 69-3, 2015 IFMA / Sportswoman of the Year, 2014 International World Games Association / Athlete of the Month (June), 2008 IFMA / Best Female Fighter (57kg)

Ranks in any martial arts styles? Second Dan black belt in taekwondo

Favorite grappling technique: Chokes

Favorite Striking technique: Spinning Back Kick

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training 11 years ago in Columbus, OH. I’ve always been aggressive growing up, even got kicked out of schools for fighting. When I was presented with the concept of training it was something I knew I really wanted to do.

Training: Wake up in the morning and go straight to the gym for whatever my first session is. After training I always try to help clean the mats and spend time with my trainers and team. Normally drive about an hour to my next location for more training. Then park it for either another training session or drive to another location to make something else happen in the day for training. I’ve always trained 2-4 times a day since I’ve started training.

What ranks and titles have you held? LFA champion, brown belt in Jiu-Jitsu, 2X Pan American champion, 7X American National champion, 5X World medalist…the list goes on.

Do you have any heroes? The Rock. He’s an amazing role model.

What would it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It would be my life’s dream coming true. It would be everything I’ve sacrificed for the last 10 years. Sleeping in gyms, trading family time for fight time and traveling for tournaments. The times I slept in my car to be able to compete and travel. Honoring my father who was my biggest fan and believed in me. As he was sick and dying, I was taking care of him and still trying to fight at the same time. Once he passed, I moved to LA and dedicated my every ounce to finally making this dream a reality. It would be honoring all the people who I influence and being able to share how they can accomplish greatness if only they care enough to get after their dreams. This is a living, breathing dream that would actually be everything to me and all the people I’ve ever met. 

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to college a few times and never finished anything. Once for massage therapy and another time for international trades 

What was your job before you started fighting? Stripper 

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Tuff-N-Uff Champion

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? LFA Champion

Favorite grappling technique: Armbar

Favorite Striking technique: Kicks

When and why did you start training for fighting? Growing up in a place like Southgate, you going to need to know how to fight, so I figured I'd get good at it at least to start with.

Training: HARD! I start the day off with boxing work and coach Jamal. Then some drilling at California Mixed Martial Arts with my UWFxUSA teammates before practice. Team training at CMMA with whatever is on the menu for the day. Later a run or strength work then off to sling booze and pizza at The Bowery. Oh, and constantly eating all day!

What ranks and titles have you held? LXF Bantamweight Champion, Super Fight League America Bantamweight Champion, DEEP Bantamweight Champion, 2018 Billy Robinson Invitational Weight class and Open weight Champion (Catch Wrestling), King of Catch 2021 Weight class and Open weight Champion (Catch Wrestling)

Do you have any heroes? Godzilla. The Pillsbury Doughboy, as he seems to be immortal.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It's a benchmark type goal and even though I have fought and beaten guys in the UFC and all over the world, the UFC is the place with the highest recognition. Plus it’s going to help me afford getting my '70 Cutlass finished. Cars are expensive and fast cars even more so.

What was your job before you started fighting? Still have one - bartender/bouncer. But before that I've worked as a dish washer, smog technician, ride operator at Knott's Berry Farm, and generally a rapscallion.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Undefeated in RIZIN and undefeated in Russia, fought for the King of Pancrase title.

If any, list ranks in any martial arts styles: Black Belt in TKD, Black Belt in BJJ

Favorite grappling technique: The ones that make 'em scream when they tap.

Favorite Striking technique: The shin to chin

When and why did you start training for fighting? It's the fight of my life, I did everything in my power to achieve victory.

What professional titles have you held? Fury FC Interim Champion

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Wako World Cup Champion in 2014, Wako Pan American Champion in 2017

Any belts/ranks in grappling disciplines? Black Belt in BJJ

Any belts/ranks in striking disciplines? Black Belt in Kickboxing, Brown Belt in Karate

What does it mean to you to fight in the UFC? Since I was very young, it’s been my dream to fight in the biggest event in the world, which is the UFC. I’m fulfilling my dream.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Daniel Cormier, because of his versatility.

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? With myself, every day striving to be better than the day before.

Is there a cause you’d like to use your platform for? No specific cause, but I’d like to motivate kids from my neighborhood to persevere in their dreams, have faith in God, and know that with hard work, dreams come true.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I studied kinesiology, I was one year away from finishing my degree.

What was your job before you started fighting? I've worked as a supermarket packer, unloading trucks, and delivering food. Recently, I've been teaching classes. And I've also done odd weekend jobs.

Favorite grappling technique: Armbar

Favorite striking technique: Spinning kick

Origin of nickname: The truth is that it has no relation to fights. When I was little I liked to paint and scratch in the street, and I chose Psicosis to scratch and paint in the street.

Personal Life / Background: In recent years, I’ve been training in Miami. I share a place with my wife, who is also a fighter, and we train almost full-time. When we can, we like to spend time at the beach. When I have the chance to travel to Chile, I enjoy spending time with family and friends. Going out to eat is my favorite hobby. I am the oldest of 7 siblings, and I was raised by my grandparents and two of my siblings. 

What’s one thing you want UFC fans around the world to know about you? I come from the end of the world, from Chile, chasing my dream. I’ve worked hard through ups and downs, but my faith in God remains strong. Today I thank God for rewarding me with this opportunity.

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I’ve had a long history of martial arts in my life. I studied Kung Fu from age 11 to 14. Later as an adult I decided to get back into it and quickly found I wanted something more real than point sparring. I wanted to really challenge myself and so I tried my hand at boxing and wrestling. Eventually I landed at an MMA gym and never looked back. My first amateur fight was an amazing experience and solidified my desire to keep pressing forward.

What ranks and titles have you held? I’ve won various grappling tournaments. I’m a purple belt in BJJ. I have a black belt in My Jhong Law Horn Kung Fu. I won an amateur IKF world Muay Thai belt in 2016. I had two amateur title belts for a local Louisiana promotion in both the 125 and 135 divisions.

Do you have any heroes? Our brave first responders and the military men and women that serve this country. I have a brother and sister-in-law that both served in Afghanistan. My husband has been a law enforcement officer for over 20 years. These are the real heroes of our day.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It’s the culmination of everything I’ve been working so hard for the past five or six years. I want to be the best and fight the best. With a look at my record, anyone can see that I haven’t shied away from the difficult fights. I’ve taken the best of what has been offered to me and I have not padded my record like so many others. I have what it takes, and a contract gives me the opportunity to compete with the best in the world and show why I will be one of the best female fighters in the world.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to LSU in Shreveport and have a degree in Spanish. I love to travel and learn from and about other languages and cultures.

What was your job before you started fighting? High school Spanish teacher

Favorite grappling technique: RNC

Favorite Striking technique: Side kick

TRAINING: A typical day of training for me is the morning pro team session at Alliance MMA. Live wrestling, drills, technique, small glove sparring. Then live sparring rounds, 2 morning sessions per week. Evening sessions are either strength and conditioning, pad work or drilling with a teammate. I also squeeze in a treadmill sprint circuit twice a week.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I have studied martial arts most of my life. I came across BJJ about six or seven years ago and fell in love. I started competing and dominated. I wanted to try my hand at the real thing and was very successful with MMA too. So it all just snowballed for me.

What ranks and titles have you held? None

Do you have any heroes? Bruce Lee, Elvis Presley, Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? Being able to support my family financially. Feeling like I am worth something to be in the most elite fighting organization on the planet. Recognition. Having the ability to inspire and reach a larger audience, as well as entertain.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? No

What was your job before you started fighting? Construction and commercial painter.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? Victorian and Pan Pacific BJJ champion and gold medalist.

Ranks in any martial arts styles: BJJ Purple belt under Carlos Viera

Favorite grappling technique: Double leg slam, RNC

Favorite striking technique: Multiple techniques

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training MMA at 23/24 because I missed the competition aspect of wrestling. You learn a lot of things about yourself from competing, some good, some bad.

What professional titles have you held? I was the Featherweight champion for Front Street Fights back in Boise, ID and just recently won the Bantamweight Championship for United Fight League.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? I was 8-1 as an amateur boxer and as a senior in high school I took first at the state tournament.

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? World’s Most Dangerous Purple belt in BJJ

Any belts/ ranks in striking disciplines? Just a few championship medals and trophies from my amateur boxing days.

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? It's hard to define tough. My third fight in the UFC against Chris Gutierrez was tough in terms of damage and I could only see through one eye. My fight where I won the featherweight championship at Front Street was very tough outside of the cage because my roommate/friend had just recently passed from a car accident, and I had a knee surgery a couple weeks before the fight.

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career and why?  This is the fight. I've had a lot of great moments throughout my career, and some not so great. But getting the job done May 2 is the only thing that matters.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Cousin Ricky Simon But all time? Frankie Edgar for MMA. Roy Jones Jr. for boxing. 

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My Mom, RIP.

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? My cause is representing people who don’t have many opportunities where they’re from. I didn’t come from much, so if I can give someone belief to chase what lights them up, that’s what matters to me.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? My motivation seems to shift from fight to fight but right now it’s simple. Set my family up for the future, prove who I am to myself and embracing the challenge I chose.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?  I went to Boise State University for one semester where I was studying sports psychology. Family matters led me to dropping out early unfortunately. 

What was your job before you started fighting? Before and during the first part of my MMA career I was involved in sales and management.

Origin of nickname: I use my middle name Vandetta as my nickname, so every time, I’m just announced by my full name.

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Fighting is pretty well my life, even my wife Shino VanHoose trains and competes. But I do have an English bulldog, his name is Atlas and a cat named Andy. Got a few hobbies, I collect some trading cards and comic books (mostly X-Men). Fully embracing the nerd I am. I also dabble in some video games. Mostly some retro stuff from childhood. I am one of 13 siblings (including step siblings). We all grew up in the small town of around 10,000 people in Ontario, OR. In my free time away from the gym I train people in MMA and self-defense. I also run an app called React Workouts, which is essentially a virtual boxing/MMA coach. It gives custom call outs during a round at random intervals {combinations, defensive actions, movements, etc).

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started to train Jiu-Jitsu in 1998 at the age of 14. I started training on and off for fighting in 2004, when I moved to California to train/teach at Cesar Gracie's Academy. Having many high level guys around (such as David Terrell, Jake Shields and the Diaz Brothers), made me want to fight as well. I didn't really take MMA seriously until I got cut from the UFC for the first time though. I was so used to performing at the highest level in BJJ/Grappling, so it was hard for me to accept that I wasn't getting the results that I believed I could get also in MMA. That's when I decided to move to Las Vegas and dedicate myself full-time into MMA training. 

What titles have you held? 3x BJJ World Champion (Gi), 2007 No Gi BJJ World Champion, 2009 ADCC Worlds Bronze Medalist (-99kg division and Absolute Division), 2011 ADCC Worlds Gold Medalist (Over 99kg Division, beating Fabricio Werdum in the Final), M-1 Challenge Light Heavyweight Champion (MMA)

qna.value:
When and why did you start training for fighting? I started in martial arts when I was a kid because people beat me up a lot, so I started at the gym to learn how to defend myself, and also to earn money.

Who are your main training partners? Besides my coaches, I only have one training partner. His name is Júnior Lobão. He’s the only one who’s been able to handle the pressure of standing in front of LokDog during an intense camp.

What ranks and titles have you held? I was the two-time UAE Warriors champion.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? I am my own favorite fighter, because I became everything no one ever imagined someone could be.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? Yes. My hero is Rafael Sombra. He saved me from a dark hole that I put myself into.

What do you consider the key fight of your career and why? All my fights are important, but the most important one was probably my fight on the Contender Series. That was the turning point between achieving my dream of entering the UFC or walking away from everything and moving on as a normal person.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked on construction sites, I was a driver, I sold DVDs on the street. I managed as I could.

Specific accomplishments in amateur competition? I did around 30 amateur fights and I had only two losses; the rest were wins.

What are your current ranks in martial arts? I’m a brown belt in jiu-jitsu and hold a black prajied Muay Thai rank. That’s more than enough.

Favorite grappling technique: Attack legs

Favorite Striking technique: Hook

Is there a cause you want to use your platform for? I want to create projects to help take kids off the wrong path and also help families in need. I believe that over time social media will help me make that happen.

Beyond a championship or money, what motivates you? Honestly, the belt doesn’t motivate me as much as money does. Money is what will support my family and give my parents a comfortable life. After money, what motivates me is what I’ll be able to build with it.

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Even outside of fighting, I’m still a fighter. I can’t escape that. I try to live a lighter life with my family, my wife, my daughter (1-year-old), one dog, and two birds. I still pressure myself for not spending enough time with them, but I’m not able to live a normal life like most people yet. I spend most of my time training and living an athletic lifestyle, and when I get home it’s already late. But with the little time I have, I always try to give them my best. Maybe after I make a few million, I’ll allow myself the luxury of enjoying life a bit more.
